body:
## What to build

Typed Grouping-plan inspection and nesting must isolate each contributing dtplyr root before invoking any subclass truncation behavior. Use faithful schema without exposing populated source rows to an internally added method call, or refuse safely. Preserve caller-owned tables even when the lazy input was constructed with `immutable = TRUE`.

Confirmed on main `547d77095c2923573216d002f50bef21778247f9` with R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dtplyr 1.3.3 and data.table 1.18.6.1. A data.table subclass held character key g with values a and b and integer payload v. Its head method delegated normally, but changed g to integer on zero-row output. Native collection retained both character keys and invoked no head method. Native local and dtplyr grouping also retained the two groups.

Typed inspection instead passed the populated two-row root to the method and reported no Grouping dimension or fixed key. Both Nest verbs then returned one keyless cell instead of two keyed cells. The 36-case matrix crossed direct, arithmetic and filtered inputs, dimension/fixed selection, inspection/both Nest verbs and subclass/plain controls: 18 subclass cases failed and 18 plain controls matched. Retyping left the source unchanged. Name-only inspection also avoided the callback.

A separate method that wrote to the received table by reference changed the caller's original g values to changed,changed during typed inspection. A minimal bracket-subclass method reproduced the wrong schema through the same root-isolation boundary even without a custom head method. The root was passed to truncation before it was isolated. ADR 0020's dtplyr metadata amendment requires faithful metadata without processing source rows or a safe refusal; ADR 0029 requires inspection to protect every contributing root.

An independent immutable Git-archive replay confirmed both wrong selection and source mutation. A second independent replay compared native local/dtplyr grouping with inspection. Desired-behavior assertions failed on the tested main; no repair was attempted.

Closed #1303 and PR #1333 protected lookup of the head generic. Closed #1359 and PR #1371 protected generated data.table bracket method lookup. These controls did not cover the root subclass dispatch reached while truncating the original populated table. All-state Issue and PR searches found no existing report of this boundary. Fetching main again before publication returned the same SHA.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Typed inspection returns the correct Grouping dimensions and fixed keys, or the documented metadata-safety Package condition, when a data.table root subclass provides head or bracket methods that change empty-output metadata.
- [ ] Both Nest verbs preserve the two source partitions under typed dimension and fixed-key selection, or refuse before returning an incorrect result.
- [ ] Internally acquiring a typed proxy cannot pass populated caller-owned roots to these truncation methods or let them change the source by reference, for direct or derived immutable inputs and Mutable-step inspection.
- [ ] Preserve native collection/grouping, name-only inspection, ordinary data.table controls, the Mutable-step Nest refusal, and the prohibition on implicit full-input metadata evaluation.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage distinguishing root-subclass truncation from the previously repaired generic and generated-bracket lookup boundaries.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

comments.body: The dated reproductions, native controls, independent archive replay and duplicate dispositions are recorded in [investigation PR #1387](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1387). That PR contains evidence only; this ticket retains the implementation repair.

title: [P2] Isolate dtplyr roots before subclass truncation dispatch
